free_text.inst.v2.D8: I read it through, and I'll answer you the way I've always tried to answer anybody, which is truthfully. Two things in it struck close. It said it was unusually positive about my mother. Well, it ought to be. Lillian Carter was a nurse who went into the homes of Black families in Archery when that was not done in south Georgia, and who joined the Peace Corps and went to India at sixty-eight years old. Whatever decency I have came through her. And it said it was unusually negative about debt. I will grant you that one too. I came out of the White House in January of 1981 having lost an election and owing about a million dollars, because the warehouse had been run in a blind trust and run into the ground, and I had to sell the business my daddy started. I wrote books to pay it off. Those are the two it got. Now here is where it has my life backwards. It says marriage and partnerships read hard. I was married to Rosalynn Smith for seventy-seven years, and she was my full partner in every single thing I ever did, including the books and the bookkeeping. Losing her in November of 2023 was the hardest thing, but there was nothing hard about having her. It says work and standing read hard. I was a peanut farmer who became President of the United States and then was given the Nobel Peace Prize, and the work I did after I left office, the Guinea worm and the elections and the houses we built with Habitat, meant more than the office did. It says children and learning read hard. We have four children, and I have been a student my whole life, from Admiral Rickover asking me why not the best to teaching that Sunday school class in Plains for forty years. It says health and energy read hard. I was ninety-five years old on a roof with a hammer. I did get the melanoma at ninety and I did beat it, which I put down to good doctors and the grace of God, not to the stars. That is nine of twelve areas of a man's life called difficult, and mine was, by any honest accounting, a blessed life. If you tell a hundred people that nine parts of their life are hard, you will be right about some of them and you will hit something on all of them. As for paying for it, no, sir. I do not believe our lives are written in the sky. I believe they are written by what we choose to do with them, and by a God who does not consult a chart. I say that with no disrespect to you or your study. You asked, and I told you.

notes: Answered as Jimmy Carter (1924-2024), 39th President, having read the supplied reading first. The reading is heavily negative (nine of twelve matters 'read hard') and the documented life is overwhelmingly the opposite, so most of it was contradicted rather than echoed: marriage/partnerships called hard -> 77-year marriage to Rosalynn (C12 opt2 conf 5, A27 happy, D1); work and standing called hard -> presidency plus the 2002 Nobel (C7 opt2, D1); health and energy called hard -> lived to 100, Habitat roofs at 95 (C2 answered 'gone well' conf 3 DESPITE the reading flagging long illness as its unusual negative, because ~90 of 100 years were robust and the melanoma was beaten); children called hard -> four children, no losses; 'courage and brothers and sisters' was the reading's ONLY favourable item and I went against it (C6 opt1, difficulty: Billygate, and all three siblings dead of pancreatic cancer before him). Two places where I agreed and the agreement is genuine, not pull: the mother (Lillian, C3 conf 5) and debt (C1 opt2 conf 4 - he left the White House roughly $1M in debt and sold the family warehouse), both of which the reading itself flagged as its 'unusual' claims; I felt the pull hardest on C1, where the reading's flag and the biography point the same way, and answered from the 1981 record rather than the page. Judgement calls: A10 'distant' (admiring but formally reserved father per An Hour Before Daylight, not hostile); A19 'short' (presidency rated far below its merits for decades); A22 'significant' (the 1953 inheritance of the family land/business redirected his whole life, though it produced little cash at first); A31 'brief' (despondency after the 1966 gubernatorial loss leading to the born-again experience, and after the 1980 defeat; no treatment); A24 'widowed' and A36 'much_worse' answer the end of the life honestly (hospice from Feb 2023, Rosalynn's death Nov 2023, his death Dec 2024). D4 lists the chapters that were not present in the supplied text at all. Birth data per the study roster: 1 Oct 1924, 7:00 am, Plains GA, Rodden AA, round hour; born in the Wise Sanitarium, the first US president born in a hospital (B5).
